therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: GABA transaminase inhibition leading to increased GABA levels
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Prevention of seizure development through enhanced GABAergic inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Infants with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex without seizures
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Cognitive Assessment Scores on Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development at 24 months

biomarker_changes: EEG biomarker for developing epilepsy assessed via epileptiform activity
subgroup_findings: Time to first clinical seizure: HR 0.593 (95% CI: 0.309–1.140), p = 0.1174
Drug resistant epilepsy at 24 months: no significant difference between groups (p = 0.4653)
Vineland-II ABC scores showed no significant difference (p = 0.1697)
safety_signals: Nervous system disorders most common serious adverse event
Respiratory disorders reported in both groups
Eye disorders reported in early vigabatrin group
Overall vigabatrin-related adverse events: 2/29 early vs 6/27 delayed
results.dose_information: 100mg/kg/day until 24 months of age or until seizures develop

context.comparator: Placebo (delayed vigabatrin) and watchful waiting control group
context.duration: 24 months treatment period with follow-up to 36 months
